questions.q: Which situation most clearly argues against a large foundation model?
options: A 5 ms latency limit on a small device
Many new products with 10 data points each
A fast prototype for a new domain

questions.q: 500,000 forecasts per day, 0.04 seconds each, machine price 3 per hour. Cost per day?
Which tool style won the M5 competition?
why: Foundation models did not exist in that form in 2020.

questions.q: A regulator wants documentation and validation of every forecasting model. Which is the harder fit?
options: A closed API model whose weights you cannot inspect or version
A LightGBM model with logged features

questions.q: Select all situations where a foundation model is a good candidate.
options: A tight 2 ms latency with rich covariates
why: No: latency and covariates argue against.

questions.q: A foundation model gives MASE 0.88 vs LightGBM 0.90, but costs 25 times more to run. What do you do?
options: Compute the value of the 0.02 gain against the extra cost; often LightGBM wins.
Use the foundation model because lower is better.
why: Accuracy alone is not the decision.

questions.q: What belongs in a written decision rule for adopting a model?
options: The model's name in the press
